info.title: Brief! API
info.description:
Backend for **Brief!**, a message board where every post fits in 255 characters.

The same API is served by two editions of the backend: **Javalin + JDBC** (`backend/`) and **Spring Boot + Spring Security + Spring Data JPA** (`backend-spring/`).

**How errors work:** error responses have an empty body. The status code carries the meaning.

**How to try the protected endpoints here:**
1. Run `POST /register` to create an account (or use one you already have).
2. Run `POST /login`. In the response headers, copy the value of `x-auth-token`.
3. Click **Authorize** at the top right, paste the token, and confirm.
4. Now `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `/messages` will work, as that account.

The app runs in *strict* mode by default: you can only post as yourself and only change your own posts. Set the environment variable `BRIEF_AUTH_MODE=compat` before starting to get the original training contract, where no token is needed.

**New in 2.1 (Spring Boot edition only):** the login token is a signed JWT; `GET /messages` and `GET /accounts/{account_id}/messages` can be read a page at a time with `limit` and `before`; in strict mode new passwords must be strong and repeated failed logins answer `429`. The Javalin edition ignores the paging parameters and always returns the full list.

**New in 2.2 (Spring Boot edition only):** mentions are stored in their own indexed table when a post is saved or edited, so `GET /accounts/{account_id}/mentions` is a look-up and no longer searches every post.

**New in 2.3 (Spring Boot edition only):** `GET /accounts/{account_id}/mentions` can be read a page at a time with `limit` and `before`, like the other lists; a username is one name whatever its capitals, for registering and for signing in; in strict mode a new username must be 3 to 30 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. The database schema is created by versioned Flyway migrations, and the application runs on PostgreSQL as well as H2.

**New in 2.4 (Spring Boot edition only):** an account has an email address. In strict mode a new account must give one, and can read but not post until the link mailed to it has been opened (`POST /email/verify`). A forgotten password is replaced through a mailed link (`POST /password/forgot`, `POST /password/reset`). An address is shown only to its own account (`GET /me`). A board can be **closed** by setting `BRIEF_INVITE_CODE`: creating an account then needs that code, and every `GET` of posts and members needs a login token. `GET /health` reports `email` and `board`, so a client knows which of this applies.

post.description:
Succeeds only if the username is allowed, the password meets the rule, and the username is not taken. The password is stored as a salted hash.

Username rule: not blank. In the Spring Boot edition in strict mode (since 2.3): 3 to 30 characters, each a letter a-z or A-Z, a digit, a dot, a dash or an underscore.

Since 2.3 (Spring Boot edition) a username is one name whatever its capitals: if `Maya` exists, `maya` and `MAYA` are taken. The name is stored and shown as it was typed.

Password rule: at least 4 characters. In the Spring Boot edition in strict mode: at least 8 characters, with at least one letter and one digit, and not the same as the username. `GET /health` reports which rule applies.

Since 2.4 (Spring Boot edition): in strict mode an `email` is required and must not belong to another account. A link is mailed to it; until it is used the account can sign in and read, and cannot post. On a closed board (`GET /health` says `"board": "closed"`) the request must carry the right `invite_code`; without it the answer is `403` whatever else the request holds, and five wrong codes from one address lock that address out for 15 minutes.

400.description: Invalid input, a username, password or email address that does not meet the rule, or a username (in any capitals) or email address that is already taken. Empty body.

403.description: Closed board: the invitation code is missing or wrong. Empty body.

429.description: Closed board: too many wrong invitation codes from this address. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. Empty body.

post.description:
Checks the username and password. Since 2.3 (Spring Boot edition) the username is matched whatever capitals are typed; the answer carries it as it was registered. The password is always exact. On success the response carries a login token in the `X-Auth-Token` header; send it back as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on write requests.

In the Spring Boot edition the token is a JWT signed with HMAC-SHA256. Its payload holds the account id (`sub`), a token id (`jti`), the issue and expiry times, and since 2.4 the account's token generation (`ver`); it is readable by anyone and holds nothing secret.

In strict mode (Spring Boot edition), five wrong passwords for the same username from the same address lock that pair out for 15 minutes. Behind a hosting platform's proxy the address is read from the header named in `BRIEF_CLIENT_IP_HEADER` (since 2.3).

Since 2.4 a token also stops working when the account's password is replaced through a mailed link: every session of that account ends at that moment.

X-Auth-Token.description: Login token, valid for 12 hours or until logout.

401.description: Username and password do not match. Empty body.

429.description: Too many failed attempts for this username from this address (Spring Boot edition, strict mode). Empty body.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until a login may be tried again.

post.description: Ends the session for the token sent. Always answers 200, even if the token is already gone (idempotent).

get.description:
Id and username only. Passwords are never included.

On a closed board (since 2.4, Spring Boot edition) this needs a login token; on an open board it is public.

401.description: Closed board (since 2.4): no token, or one that is unknown or expired. Empty body.

400.description: The id is not a number. Empty body.

401.description: Closed board (since 2.4): no token, or one that is unknown or expired. Empty body.

get.description: On a closed board (since 2.4, Spring Boot edition) this needs a login token; on an open board it is public.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Spring Boot edition. How many posts to return, newest first. If `before` is given without `limit`, 20 are returned. Example: `10`.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Spring Boot edition. Return only posts with a smaller `message_id`. Pass the id of the last post of the previous page to get the next one.

200.description: That member's messages. An empty list if there are none.

X-Has-More.description: Only when `limit` or `before` was sent: `true` if older posts exist beyond this page, otherwise `false`.

400.description: The id is not a number, or a paging parameter is out of range. Empty body.

401.description: Closed board (since 2.4): no token, or one that is unknown or expired. Empty body.

get.description:
Pages the same way as `GET /messages` when `limit` and/or `before` is sent (Spring Boot edition).

On a closed board (since 2.4, Spring Boot edition) this needs a login token; on an open board it is public.

get.summary: List posts that mention a member

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Spring Boot edition, since 2.3. How many mentions to return, newest first. If `before` is given without `limit`, 20 are returned. Example: `20`.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Spring Boot edition, since 2.3. Return only mentions in posts with a smaller `message_id`. Pass the id of the last post of the previous page to get the next one.

get.description:
Posts written by other members that contain this member's username as a whole word, in any letter case, with or without a leading `@`. A member's own posts never count.

Without query parameters: every mention, oldest first.

Spring Boot edition, since 2.3: with `limit` and/or `before`, one page, **newest first**, and an `X-Has-More` header, exactly like `GET /messages`. The web app reads 20 at a time. The Javalin edition ignores the parameters and returns the full list.

Spring Boot edition, since 2.2: who a post mentions is worked out when the post is saved or edited and stored in a `mention` table, so this request is an indexed look-up. One consequence: a name typed before that member registered is not a mention. The Javalin edition searches every post at request time.

On a closed board (since 2.4, Spring Boot edition) this needs a login token; on an open board it is public.

200.description: The mentioning messages: all of them oldest first, or one page newest first. An empty list if there are none.

X-Has-More.description: Only when `limit` or `before` was sent: `true` if older mentions exist beyond this page, otherwise `false`.

400.description: The id is not a number, or a paging parameter is out of range. Empty body.

401.description: Closed board (since 2.4): no token, or one that is unknown or expired. Empty body.

200.description: The posts. An empty list if there are none.

X-Has-More.description: Only when `limit` or `before` was sent: `true` if older posts exist beyond this page, otherwise `false`.

400.description: `limit` is not between 1 and 100, or `before` is not a positive number. Empty body.

401.description: Closed board (since 2.4): no token, or one that is unknown or expired. Empty body.

get.description:
Without parameters: every post, oldest first (the original contract).

With `limit` and/or `before` (Spring Boot edition): one page, **newest first**, and an `X-Has-More` response header. To walk the whole list, call with `limit`, then repeat with `before` set to the `message_id` of the last post you received, until `X-Has-More` is `false`.

On a closed board (since 2.4, Spring Boot edition) this needs a login token; on an open board it is public.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Spring Boot edition. How many posts to return, newest first. If `before` is given without `limit`, 20 are returned. Example: `10`.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Spring Boot edition. Return only posts with a smaller `message_id`. Pass the id of the last post of the previous page to get the next one.

post.description: The text must not be blank and must be at most 255 characters, and `posted_by` must be a real account. In strict mode `posted_by` must be the signed-in account. If `time_posted_epoch` is 0 or missing, the server uses the current time.

400.description: Invalid text or unknown author. Empty body.

401.description: Strict mode: missing, unknown or expired token. Empty body.

403.description: Strict mode: `posted_by` is not the signed-in account, or (since 2.4) the account's email address is not confirmed yet. Empty body.

200.description: The message. **If there is no such message the status is still 200 and the body is empty.**

400.description: The id is not a number. Empty body.

401.description: Closed board (since 2.4): no token, or one that is unknown or expired. Empty body.

get.description: On a closed board (since 2.4, Spring Boot edition) this needs a login token; on an open board it is public.

400.description: No such message, or the new text is blank or over 255 characters. Empty body.

401.description: Strict mode: missing, unknown or expired token. Empty body.

403.description: Strict mode: the message belongs to someone else. Since 2.4 also: the account's email address is not confirmed yet. Empty body.

delete.description: Idempotent: deleting a message that is already gone is not an error.

200.description: The deleted message, or an empty body if it did not exist.

401.description: Strict mode: missing, unknown or expired token. Empty body.

403.description: Strict mode: the message belongs to someone else. Empty body.

get.description: Since 2.4 (Spring Boot edition). The one place an email address is shown, and only to the account it belongs to. Needs a token in every mode.

401.description: Missing, unknown or expired token. Empty body.

post.summary: Give your account an email address
post.description: Since 2.4 (Spring Boot edition). Gives the account an address, or replaces one that was never confirmed, and mails the confirmation link. A confirmed address cannot be changed in 2.4. Needs a token in every mode.

400.description: Not an email address, an address another account has, or the account's address is already confirmed. Empty body.

401.description: Missing, unknown or expired token. Empty body.

403.description: The token belongs to another account. Empty body.

post.description: Since 2.4 (Spring Boot edition). A new link replaces the earlier one: only the newest mail works.

400.description: The account has no address, or it is already confirmed. Empty body.

401.description: Missing, unknown or expired token. Empty body.

429.description: The last link was mailed less than a minute ago. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. Empty body.

post.description: Since 2.4 (Spring Boot edition). The mailed link opens the web app at `/?verify=<secret>`; the app sends the secret here. Needs no token: holding the link is the proof. A link works once, for 24 hours.

200.description: The address is confirmed; the account can post. Empty body.

400.description: Unknown, used or expired link. Empty body.

post.description: Since 2.4 (Spring Boot edition). Mails a link to the address if, and only if, it is the confirmed address of an account. The answer is `200` either way, so this cannot be used to find out who has an account. At most one mail per account per minute.

200.description: Accepted, whether or not a mail was sent. Empty body.

400.description: No `email` in the request. Empty body.

429.description: Strict mode: more than five requests from one address in 15 minutes. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. Empty body.

post.summary: Set a new password with a mailed link
post.description: Since 2.4 (Spring Boot edition). The mailed link opens the web app at `/?reset=<secret>`; the app sends the secret and the new password here. A link works once, for one hour. On success every login token of the account issued before stops working. A password that is refused does not use the link up.

200.description: The password is replaced. Sign in with the new one. Empty body.

400.description: Unknown, used or expired link, or a password that does not meet the rule. Empty body.

get.description: `password_policy` is sent by the Spring Boot edition: `strong` in strict mode, `basic` in compat mode. Since 2.4 it also sends `email` (`required` in strict mode, `optional` in compat mode) and `board` (`closed` when an invitation code is set, otherwise `open`). The Javalin edition sends only `status`. This endpoint is public on a closed board too.

bearerAuth.description: Paste the `x-auth-token` value from a successful `POST /login`.

password.description: At least 4 characters; in the Spring Boot edition in strict mode at least 8 with a letter and a digit.

Account.description: The contract echoes back the password the caller sent. It is never read back from the database, which only holds a hash.

example.message_text: Not really, I just want to come in and see who's up to chat!

time_posted_epoch.description: Seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC. Send 0 to let the server fill it in.

password.description: At least 4 characters; in the Spring Boot edition in strict mode at least 8 with a letter and a digit.

email.description: Since 2.4 (Spring Boot edition). Required in strict mode, optional in compat mode. Stored in lower case. Do not send it to the Javalin edition.

invite_code.description: Since 2.4 (Spring Boot edition). Needed on a closed board, ignored on an open one.

email.description: null for an account that has not given an address.

can_post.description: false in strict mode while an address is waiting to be confirmed.

token.description: The secret from the mailed link: the text after `?verify=` or `?reset=`.
The secret from the mailed link: the text after `?reset=`.
